name: Afghanistan
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, set among rugged mountain ranges.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
Its rugged mountains have earned it the nickname 'graveyard of empires,' since invading armies have struggled to hold it for centuries.
For thousands of years, a brilliant blue gemstone mined in its mountains has been prized by artists and royalty around the world.

name: Armenia
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country tucked between two seas, in a mountainous region where two continents meet.
facts: It became the first country in the world to officially adopt Christianity as its state religion, in the year 301.
Its own alphabet, created more than 1,600 years ago, is still used to write its language today.
A famous, legendary mountain often associated with its history and an ancient flood story now sits just across its border.

name: Azerbaijan
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the western shore of a huge inland sea, with a thin detached sliver pinched between two neighbors.
facts: It's nicknamed the 'Land of Fire,' thanks to natural gas seeping from the ground that burns continuously in a few spots.
Its capital sits beside the world's largest inland body of water, often called a sea even though it's technically a lake.
Some of the first modern oil wells ever drilled on Earth were sunk into the ground here in the 1800s.

name: Bangladesh
alt: A world map with a highlighted country almost entirely surrounded by a much larger neighbor, fanning out into a river delta near a bay.
facts: It sits on the largest river delta in the world, formed where several mighty rivers spill into the sea.
It's one of the most densely populated countries on Earth, packing a huge population into a relatively small area.
A vast mangrove forest along its coast is one of the last places on Earth where tigers swim between islands to hunt.

name: Bhutan
alt: A world map with a tiny, landlocked highlighted country tucked high in a mountain range between two much larger neighbors.
facts: Instead of just tracking economic growth, its government officially measures the happiness of its people as a national goal.
It was one of the last countries in the world to allow television and the internet, only doing so in the late 1990s.
It absorbs more carbon dioxide from the air than it produces, thanks to its vast forests.

name: Brunei
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country split into two small pieces on the coast of a large tropical island, surrounded by a much bigger neighbor.
facts: Its ruler is one of the wealthiest royals in the world, thanks to vast reserves of oil and natural gas.
It shares one island with two larger neighboring countries.
Most residents here pay no income tax at all, with the government's oil wealth covering many public costs.

name: Cambodia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country in the middle of a peninsula, wrapped around a large lake fed by a great river.
facts: It's home to the largest religious monument on Earth, a sprawling temple complex built nearly a thousand years ago.
Many shops and markets here happily accept a foreign currency from across the ocean right alongside their own money.
Its ancient empire once stretched across a huge swath of the region, leaving behind hundreds of temple ruins hidden in the jungle.

name: China
alt: A world map with an enormous highlighted landmass covering much of the eastern side of a continent.
facts: It's home to one of the largest populations of any country in the world.
A wall built over centuries to defend its northern borders stretches for thousands of miles across mountains and deserts.
It's the only place on Earth where giant pandas live in the wild.

name: Cyprus
alt: A world map with a small highlighted island alone in the middle of a sea, near where three continents almost meet.
facts: It's an island split between two different communities, with a buffer zone running straight through its capital city.
Ancient myths claimed it was the birthplace of the goddess of love, rising from sea foam near its shores.
A squeaky, salty cheese that doesn't melt when grilled was invented here centuries ago.

name: Georgia
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country wedged between a sea and a towering mountain range, where two continents meet.
facts: Archaeologists believe wine was first made here more than 8,000 years ago, making it one of the oldest wine regions on Earth.
Its rugged mountain range is home to some of the tallest peaks outside of one much taller range further east.
It has a centuries-old tradition of singing in complex, multiple harmony parts at once, recognized as a treasured cultural practice.

name: India
alt: A world map with a huge highlighted landmass shaped like a triangle, jutting south into a warm ocean.
facts: It recently became the most populous country on Earth.
A board game played by millions worldwide today is believed to have first been invented here.
One of its emperors built an enormous white marble tomb for his wife that's now considered one of the most beautiful buildings on the planet.

name: Indonesia
alt: A world map with a long, scattered chain of highlighted islands stretching between two oceans, straddling the equator.
facts: It's made up of more than 17,000 islands, more than any other country on Earth.
More people who follow Islam live here than in any other country in the world.
It's the only place on Earth where you'll find giant lizards big enough to take down a deer in the wild.

name: Iran
alt: A world map with a large highlighted country between two seas, much of it covered in high desert plateau.
facts: Thousands of years ago, an empire centered here built one of the largest empires the ancient world had ever seen.
It produces more saffron, one of the world's most expensive spices, than any other country on Earth.
Ancient builders here engineered clever wind-catching towers that cooled buildings centuries before electric air conditioning existed.

name: Iraq
alt: A world map with a highlighted country in the middle of a dry region, with two great rivers running through it toward a gulf.
facts: It's often called the 'cradle of civilization,' since some of the very first cities and writing systems on Earth appeared here thousands of years ago.
One of its ancient cities was said to have legendary hanging gardens, counted among the wonders of the ancient world.
The wheel, one of humanity's most important inventions, is believed to have first been used for transportation in this region.

name: Israel
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the eastern edge of a sea, with a deep, narrow basin along part of its border.
facts: It's home to the lowest point of dry land on Earth, a salty sea so dense that swimmers float without even trying.
Three major world religions all consider one of its cities among their holiest places.
Facing a dry climate, it became a world leader in turning salty seawater into fresh drinking water.

name: Japan
alt: A world map with a long chain of highlighted islands curving along the eastern edge of a continent, surrounded entirely by ocean.
facts: It's made up of thousands of islands, though most people live on just a handful of the largest ones.
One of its family-run businesses has operated continuously for over a thousand years, making it one of the oldest companies on Earth.
Its high-speed trains travel so fast and so punctually that delays of even a minute or two make headlines.

name: Jordan
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in a dry region, with just a tiny sliver of coastline reaching a gulf.
facts: An entire ancient city here was carved directly into rose-colored cliffs more than 2,000 years ago.
Filmmakers have used its vast red desert to stand in for the surface of Mars in several movies.
Despite being mostly desert, it shares one of the saltiest, lowest bodies of water on Earth with a neighboring country.

name: Kazakhstan
alt: A world map with an enormous, landlocked highlighted country spanning the middle of a continent, partly bordering a huge inland sea.
facts: It's the largest landlocked country in the world.
One of the world's oldest and busiest spaceports sits on its steppe, launching astronauts into orbit for decades.
Horses have been central to life here for thousands of years, and fermented mare's milk is still a traditional drink.

name: Kuwait
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country at the tip of a gulf, squeezed between two much larger neighbors.
facts: It sits on some of the largest oil reserves on the planet despite its small size.
Its flat desert landscape regularly produces some of the hottest temperatures ever recorded on Earth.
Its currency is consistently ranked among the most valuable in the world, unit for unit.

name: Kyrgyzstan
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country folded into a knot of high mountains in the middle of a continent.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
More than 90 percent of its land is covered by towering mountains, leaving very little flat ground to farm.
One of its high mountain lakes is so large and deep that it almost never freezes, even in brutal winters.

name: Laos
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country shaped like a long, narrow strip down the middle of a peninsula.
facts: It's the only landlocked country in its entire region.
Its old kingdom was once known as the 'Land of a Million Elephants.'
A single great river forms much of its western border and serves as a vital highway for trade and travel.

name: Lebanon
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country along the eastern edge of a sea, backed by a narrow strip of mountains.
facts: Its flag features a cedar tree, a species so important to its history that ancient peoples once shipped its timber across the sea to build temples and ships.
An ancient seafaring civilization based here is credited with spreading one of the first widely used alphabets across the ancient world.
Despite its small size, its capital was once nicknamed after a famous European city for its lively cafes and nightlife.

name: Malaysia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country split into two separate pieces, one on a peninsula and one on a large island, divided by a stretch of sea.
facts: It's split into two separate parts, divided by a stretch of sea between a peninsula and a large island.
Twin towers built here once held the record for the tallest buildings in the world.
Its rainforests are one of the last wild homes of orangutans anywhere on Earth.

name: Mongolia
alt: A world map with a large, landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, between a vast desert and a forested north.
facts: It's one of the least densely populated countries in the world, with vast open steppe stretching in every direction.
An empire that began here in the 1200s grew into the largest contiguous land empire in history.
Many people here still live a nomadic lifestyle, herding animals and moving between traditional round tents through the seasons.

name: Myanmar
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped like a kite along the edge of a peninsula, fringed by a long coastline on a bay.
facts: One ancient city here is dotted with thousands of Buddhist temples and pagodas built over several centuries.
It produces more teak, a hardwood prized for furniture and shipbuilding, than any other country on Earth.
It was known by a different name for most of its modern history before officially changing it.

name: Nepal
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country squeezed along the southern slope of the tallest mountain range on Earth.
facts: It's home to the tallest mountain on Earth, towering far above the clouds.
It's the birthplace of a spiritual teacher whose followers now number in the hundreds of millions worldwide.
It's the only country in the world with a flag that isn't a rectangle.

name: North Korea
alt: A world map with a highlighted country occupying the northern half of a peninsula, cut off from its southern neighbor by a narrow strip.
facts: Most of its citizens have no access to the global internet, browsing only a tightly controlled internal network instead.
It's home to one of the largest stadiums in the world, built to hold well over 100,000 spectators.
Time itself briefly ran differently here, after it created its own time zone for a few years before switching back.

name: Oman
alt: A world map with a highlighted country curving along a coastline at the edge of a peninsula, with a small detached piece near a busy strait.
facts: It's considered one of the oldest continuously independent states in its entire region.
For thousands of years, traders here grew rich exporting a fragrant tree resin once worth its weight in gold.
Despite being mostly desert, one of its mountain ranges gets cool enough most years to see occasional frost.

name: Pakistan
alt: A world map with a highlighted country between a desert coastline and some of the tallest mountains on Earth.
facts: It's home to the world's second-tallest mountain, a notoriously difficult peak to climb.
One of the world's earliest great civilizations built sophisticated cities with drainage systems here more than 4,000 years ago.
It's one of the most populous countries on Earth.

name: Philippines
alt: A world map with a huge cluster of highlighted islands scattered between two seas, east of a much larger landmass.
facts: It's made up of more than 7,000 islands scattered across the sea.
Christmas celebrations here are said to be among the longest in the world, with festive songs sometimes starting as early as September.
It's hit by dozens of typhoons most years, more than almost any other country on Earth.

name: Qatar
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted peninsula jutting out into a gulf from the edge of a much larger landmass.
facts: It became the first country in the Middle East to host the world's biggest soccer tournament.
It sits on some of the largest natural gas reserves on the planet, despite its small size.
It's regularly ranked among the wealthiest countries in the world per person.

name: Saudi Arabia
alt: A world map with a vast highlighted country covering most of a peninsula, bordered by a sea on one side and a gulf on the other.
facts: It's the largest country in the world with no permanent rivers at all.
Two of the holiest cities in one of the world's major religions are located within its borders, drawing millions of pilgrims every year.
It's home to one of the largest continuous sand deserts on Earth.

name: South Korea
alt: A world map with a highlighted country occupying the southern half of a peninsula, cut off from its northern neighbor by a narrow strip.
facts: It's become a global hub for pop music, with bands here selling out stadiums on nearly every continent.
It regularly ranks among the countries with the fastest average internet speeds in the world.
A heavily guarded strip of land running along its northern border is one of the most fortified borders on Earth.

name: Sri Lanka
alt: A world map with a small, teardrop-shaped highlighted island just off the southern tip of a much larger neighboring landmass.
facts: It's shaped like a teardrop, hanging just off the southern tip of a much larger neighboring country.
Tea grown in its misty highlands is shipped and sold all over the world under an older name for the island.
Engineers here built enormous reservoirs and canals more than a thousand years ago to capture monsoon rains.

name: Syria
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the eastern edge of a sea, mostly dry plains rising toward mountains in the west.
facts: Its capital is considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
For thousands of years, it sat at a crossroads where major trade routes between three continents all met.
One of its cities has produced a distinctive olive oil soap using the same traditional process for centuries.

name: Tajikistan
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country almost entirely covered by jagged, snow-capped mountains.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
More than 90 percent of its land is covered by towering mountains, including a range nicknamed the 'roof of the world.'
It's one of the most mountainous countries that used to be part of a much larger union of republics.

name: Thailand
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped like an elephant's head, stretching down a narrow peninsula.
facts: It's the only country in its region that was never colonized by a European power.
Its capital is consistently ranked among the most-visited cities in the world.
Elephants are such an important national symbol here that one used to appear on its flag.

name: Timor-Leste
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country on the eastern end of an island shared with a much larger neighbor.
facts: It's one of the newest countries in the world, gaining full independence only in the early 2000s.
It shares one island with a much larger neighboring country, splitting it roughly in two.
Most people here are Catholic, a legacy of European colonizers who ruled for centuries, unlike most of its mostly Muslim or Buddhist neighbors.

name: Turkey
alt: A world map with a highlighted country spanning a narrow strait between two continents, bordered by sea on three sides.
facts: It's split between two continents, joined by bridges and tunnels across a narrow strait.
Its largest city is the only city in the world that sits on two continents at once.
One of its regions is dotted with tall, cone-shaped rock formations, some hollowed out into homes and churches centuries ago.

name: Turkmenistan
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country along the eastern shore of a huge inland sea, mostly covered by desert.
facts: A natural gas crater here has been burning continuously since the 1970s, earning it a fiery nickname.
Much of its land is covered by a vast desert that takes up most of the country.
Its capital city is filled with so many white marble buildings that it holds a record for the largest concentration of marble-clad buildings in the world.

name: United Arab Emirates
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the southern shore of a gulf, at the edge of a vast desert peninsula.
facts: It's home to the tallest building in the world, piercing far above any cloud in the sky.
It's made up of seven separate emirates joined together as one federation.
Engineers here built artificial islands shaped like palm trees, visible even from space.

name: Uzbekistan
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries.
facts: It's one of only two countries in the entire world that are landlocked and also entirely surrounded by other landlocked countries.
Ancient cities here once thrived as major stops along a famous network of trade routes connecting Asia and Europe.
Some of its city squares are lined with dazzling tiled mosques and monuments built centuries ago by powerful Silk Road rulers.

name: Vietnam
alt: A world map with a long, S-shaped highlighted country curving down the eastern edge of a peninsula.
facts: It's shaped like a long, curving 'S' stretching along its coast.
Motorbikes vastly outnumber cars on its streets, weaving through traffic in massive numbers.
It's home to the largest cave passage in the world, big enough to fit skyscrapers inside.

name: Yemen
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the southern tip of a peninsula, with a small detached island far out in a nearby sea.
facts: One of its remote islands is home to bizarre, umbrella-shaped trees found growing wild nowhere else on Earth.
One of its ancient walled cities is packed with centuries-old mudbrick towers so tall and dense it's nicknamed the 'Manhattan of the desert.'
Ancient legends linked it to a wealthy and powerful queen famous in stories across multiple religions.
